items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: And Mike Moore, and John Bunch. So we just threw it together. It came out great.

ctx.x: You had a couple of albums under your own name off and on?

Yeah I did. One was a mistake. That was called “Jake Takes Manhattan” and it was supposed to be with Rosemary Clooney, although she didn’t show she got sick. And so we just put it together as an album. It was all off the top of my head. We never rehearsed a note. But we did it as we went along. Carmen Leggio, a very, very fine player on that. Danny Stiles. Guys you never heard. But it was the first and sometimes the only record date with that company. And Mike Moore, and John Bunch. So we just threw it together.…

items.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: And I showed them to, I think it was Jake Hanna or somebody, and he said, “My, those are wonderful cymbals,”

ctx.x: I’m just off on this sideline. John you were talking about some of the people that had great stories that we talked to. And you mentioned Milt Hinton and Doc Cheatham. I take it that you know some of those stories? Do you? Would you share any of them?

Well I can’t think of many stories in relation to those two. I’m not a very good, I don’t have a very good memory. As far as, I was just telling some people today you know I also worked with Gene Krupa quite a lot in the quartet. With Charlie Ventura. He was one of the great guys, one of the nicest guys, personally. The complete opposite from these three guys that I worked long periods of time on.
